title: Practice 8: Which prefix? — the whole table, as practice

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: A cockroach has climbed up on me!
exercises.why: **залез** is the past tense (masculine) of **залезть** (to climb up (finished action); (also figurative) to get into, to scramble) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **залезать**. past: он зале́з · она зале́зла · оно зале́зло · они зале́зли. — Wiktionary, «залезть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "за-" implies the following meaning: (a) Getting (disappearing) behind something — заходить, зайти за + Acc.: Солнце заходит за облака. Автомашина заезжает за дом. (b) Dropping in on somebody or stopping by at a certain place: заходить, зайти — в магазин, на почту, к учителю. (c) Dropping in or stopping by to fetch something or someone — заходить, зайти за + Instr.: Я зайду за вами. — I'll stop by to pick you up. Он зашёл за книгой. — He dropped in to pick up the book. Also note the combination of subparagraphs (b) and (c): Он зашёл ко мне за книгой. — He stopped by at my place to pick up the book. Я заехал на почту за письмами. — I stopped by at the post office to get my mail.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **влез** (**влезть**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **вылез** (**вылезть**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **слез** (**слезть**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The water came up to our necks.
exercises.why: **дошла** is the past tense (feminine) of **дойти** (to go to, to come to, to arrive at, to reach; to come down to) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **доходить**. past: он дошёл · она дошла́ · оно дошло́ · они дошли́. — Wiktionary, «дойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**до-** — Reaching a limit or destination Example: Пассажиры доехали до последней остановки и вышли из автобуса. — The passengers reached the last station and exited the bus. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «"Going verbs" with prefix "до-" indicate motion up to a certain point and may mean: a) going as far as …; b) reaching of a destination. Я доехал до угла и повернул направо. (went as far as…) У меня было мало бензина, но я всё-таки доехал до города. (reached the destination) These verbs are always followed by the preposition до + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  Compare: «Танки дошли до леса.» (Perfective, past) — DLI, Lesson 62. «Когда вы дойдёте до почты, поверните направо.» (future) — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **вышла** (**выйти**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **обошла** (**обойти**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **подошла** (**подойти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: I've decided to tell on Tom.
exercises.why: **донести** (the infinitive) (to carry (to, as far as), to bring (to), to deliver; to report, to announce, to inform) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **доносить**. — Wiktionary, «донести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**до-** — Reaching a limit or destination Example: Пассажиры доехали до последней остановки и вышли из автобуса. — The passengers reached the last station and exited the bus. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «"Going verbs" with prefix "до-" indicate motion up to a certain point and may mean: a) going as far as …; b) reaching of a destination. Я доехал до угла и повернул направо. (went as far as…) У меня было мало бензина, но я всё-таки доехал до города. (reached the destination) These verbs are always followed by the preposition до + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **перенести** (**перенести**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **поднести** (**поднести**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **пронести** (**пронести**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: We'll put you on the list.
exercises.why: **внесем** is the future tense (1st person plural) of **внести** (to carry in, to bring in; to pay in, to deposit) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **вносить**. future: я внесу́ · ты внесёшь · он внесёт · мы внесём · вы внесёте · они внесу́т. — Wiktionary, «внести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **поднесём** (**поднести**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **принесём** (**принести**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion; **унесём** (**унести**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The bird escaped from its cage.
exercises.why: **сбежала** is the past tense (feminine) of **сбежать** (to run down (from); to run away, to make off, to flee, to break out) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **сбегать**. past: он сбежа́л · она сбежа́ла · оно сбежа́ло · они сбежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «сбежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. Он сходит вниз по лестнице. (b) to come off, to drive off: Автомобиль съехал с дороги. Поезд сошёл с пути. Note that these verbs (сходить, съезжать, etc.) are usually followed by the preposition с + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **отбежала** (**отбежать**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **подбежала** (**подбежать**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **пробежала** (**пробежать**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: She's a little slow on the uptake.
exercises.why: **доходит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **доходить** (to come to, to arrive at, to reach (usually by foot); (by extension) to finally or eventually get to, to achieve some state or condition) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **дойти**. present: я дохожу́ · ты дохо́дишь · он дохо́дит · мы дохо́дим · вы дохо́дите · они дохо́дят. — Wiktionary, «доходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**до-** — Reaching a limit or destination Example: Пассажиры доехали до последней остановки и вышли из автобуса. — The passengers reached the last station and exited the bus. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «"Going verbs" with prefix "до-" indicate motion up to a certain point and may mean: a) going as far as …; b) reaching of a destination. Я доехал до угла и повернул направо. (went as far as…) У меня было мало бензина, но я всё-таки доехал до города. (reached the destination) These verbs are always followed by the preposition до + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  Compare: «Мы обычно доходим до этой остановки, а дальше едем на трамвае.» (Imperfective, present) — DLI, Lesson 62. «Во время дождей вода доходила до нашего дома.» (past) — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **переходит** (**переходить**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **приходит** (**приходить**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion; **проходит** (**проходить**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The house was carried away by the flood.
exercises.why: **унесло** is the past tense (neuter) of **унести** (to take away, to take off, to carry (away); (figuratively) to take (a life), to claim (a life)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уносить**. past: он унёс · она унесла́ · оно унесло́ · они унесли́. — Wiktionary, «унести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «уносить — унести — to take (carry) away.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choices: **внесло** (**внести**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **поднесло** (**поднести**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **пронесло** (**пронести**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Tom escaped easily.
exercises.why: **сбежал** is the past tense (masculine) of **сбежать** (to run down (from); to run away, to make off, to flee, to break out) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **сбегать**. past: он сбежа́л · она сбежа́ла · оно сбежа́ло · они сбежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «сбежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. Он сходит вниз по лестнице. (b) to come off, to drive off: Автомобиль съехал с дороги. Поезд сошёл с пути. Note that these verbs (сходить, съезжать, etc.) are usually followed by the preposition с + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **вбежал** (**вбежать**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **выбежал** (**выбежать**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **добежал** (**добежать**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: I'll come on Monday.
exercises.why: **приду** is the future tense (1st person singular) of **прийти** (to come (to), to arrive (at)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приходить**. future: я приду́ · ты придёшь · он придёт · мы придём · вы придёте · они приду́т. — Wiktionary, «прийти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choices: **дойду** (**дойти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **подойду** (**подойти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **уйду** (**уйти**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: I walked out of the movie.
exercises.why: **вышел** is the past tense (masculine) of **выйти** (to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выходить**. past: он вы́шел · она вы́шла · оно вы́шло · они вы́шли. — Wiktionary, «выйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  The other choices: **вошёл** (**войти**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **пришёл** (**прийти**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion; **прошёл** (**пройти**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The train was derailed.
exercises.why: **сошёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **сойти** (to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off; (figuratively) to come off, to disappear, to go from) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **сходить**. past: он сошёл · она сошла́ · оно сошло́ · они сошли́. — Wiktionary, «сойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. Он сходит вниз по лестнице. (b) to come off, to drive off: Автомобиль съехал с дороги. Поезд сошёл с пути. Note that these verbs (сходить, съезжать, etc.) are usually followed by the preposition с + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **вошёл** (**войти**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **зашёл** (**зайти**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **пришёл** (**прийти**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: I'll drive you somewhere.
exercises.why: **отвезу** is the future tense (1st person singular) of **отвезти** (to take away (by vehicle), to drive away, to take (someone or something by vehicle)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **отвозить**. future: я отвезу́ · ты отвезёшь · он отвезёт · мы отвезём · вы отвезёте · они отвезу́т. — Wiktionary, «отвезти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под- Example: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца, который предложил ему конфеты. — The boy stepped back from the stranger who had offered him candy. Prepositional phrases: от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Verbs of motion with the prefix от- denote moving away from an object, a place or a person and require the preposition от + genitive case: Я отхожу от автомобиля. Студент отходит от учителя. Грузовик отъезжает от магазина.» — DLI, Lesson 29.  «отвозить — отвезти — to take (haul) to отводить — отвести — to take (lead) to. Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there". Thus:.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there".» — DLI, Lesson 79.  Compare: «Я отвёз деньги в банк.» (I took (by vehicle) money to the bank.) — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choices: **ввезу** (**ввезти**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **подвезу** (**подвезти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **привезу** (**привезти**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Let's go out on the balcony.
exercises.why: **выйдем** is the future tense (1st person plural) of **выйти** (to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выходить**. future: я вы́йду · ты вы́йдешь · он вы́йдет · мы вы́йдем · вы вы́йдете · они вы́йдут. — Wiktionary, «выйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  The other choices: **зайдём** (**зайти**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **перейдём** (**перейти**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **пройдём** (**пройти**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: A fly got into the apartment.
exercises.why: **влетела** is the past tense (feminine) of **влететь** (to fly into; (colloquial) to run into (to enter while running), to burst into) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **влетать**. past: он влете́л · она влете́ла · оно влете́ло · они влете́ли. — Wiktionary, «влететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **облетела** (**облететь**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **отлетела** (**отлететь**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **пролетела** (**пролететь**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Tom leaves for Barcelona by plane.
exercises.why: **улетает** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **улетать** (to fly away, to depart (by flying); (figuratively) to be carried away or transported in thoughts or feelings) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **улететь**. present: я улета́ю · ты улета́ешь · он улета́ет · мы улета́ем · вы улета́ете · они улета́ют. — Wiktionary, «улетать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choices: **влетает** (**влетать**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **долетает** (**долетать**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **залетает** (**залетать**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: I will marry you.
exercises.why: **выйду** is the future tense (1st person singular) of **выйти** (to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выходить**. future: я вы́йду · ты вы́йдешь · он вы́йдет · мы вы́йдем · вы вы́йдете · они вы́йдут. — Wiktionary, «выйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  The other choices: **дойду** (**дойти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **зайду** (**зайти**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **перейду** (**перейти**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Mayuko entered the room.
exercises.why: **вошла** is the past tense (feminine) of **войти** (to enter, to go in(to) (by foot), to get in(to); to penetrate into) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **входить**. past: он вошёл · она вошла́ · оно вошло́ · они вошли́. — Wiktionary, «войти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  Compare: «Я вошёл в комнату и открыл окно.» (Perfective) — DLI, Lesson 56. «Я войду в комнату и открою окно.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  The other choices: **дошла** (**дойти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **отошла** (**отойти**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **прошла** (**пройти**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The custom originated in China.
exercises.why: **исходит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **исходить** ((imperfective only) to issue (from), to come (from), to originate (from), to emanate (from); (imperfective only) to proceed (from), to base oneself (on))) — imperfective. present: я исхожу́ · ты исхо́дишь · он исхо́дит · мы исхо́дим · вы исхо́дите · они исхо́дят. — Wiktionary, «исходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**из-, изо-, ис-** — Movement involving the entire area concerned and carried out in all directions; only formed from multidirectional verb of motion Example: Я изъездил весь мир. — I traveled over the whole world. Prepositional phrases: without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **входит** (**входить**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **выходит** (**выходить**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **уходит** (**уходить**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: The baby crept into the room.
exercises.why: **заполз** is the past tense (masculine) of **заползти** (to crawl into) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **заползать**. past: он запо́лз · она заползла́ · оно заползло́ · они заползли́. — Wiktionary, «заползти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "за-" implies the following meaning: (a) Getting (disappearing) behind something — заходить, зайти за + Acc.: Солнце заходит за облака. Автомашина заезжает за дом. (b) Dropping in on somebody or stopping by at a certain place: заходить, зайти — в магазин, на почту, к учителю. (c) Dropping in or stopping by to fetch something or someone — заходить, зайти за + Instr.: Я зайду за вами. — I'll stop by to pick you up. Он зашёл за книгой. — He dropped in to pick up the book. Also note the combination of subparagraphs (b) and (c): Он зашёл ко мне за книгой. — He stopped by at my place to pick up the book. Я заехал на почту за письмами. — I stopped by at the post office to get my mail.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **вполз** (**вползти**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **выполз** (**выползти**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **подполз** (**подползти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
